description: Residual carve-out from fz-kdt.97 (2026-08-31, 86afa1db7), recorded by the builder and deliberately not closed there: an ExecutableReturn in a recursion component that returns a CALLABLE stands aside from contract_transport_layout -- a clause set has no lane contract, and the row its demand names is fact-derived by exact_direct_callable_layout (the fz-9i4.4.5 one-authority carrier; forcing the contract broke compiler2_transport_plan_preserves_recursive_callable_return_identity, the make(n) -> make(n-1) closure-returning recursion). Consequence: a recursion cycle returning a callable can still publish disagreeing return forms and lose tail form (Continue) on those edges. No fixture currently measures a hot callable-returning recursion, so the cost is unquantified. Commented at the carve-out site. Fix direction, if it ever matters: a callable-aware contract (the boxed apply seam is the natural agreed form -- both sides already box at the boundary), measured against the identity-preservation test. Sequenced with fz-kdt.96 (both are callable-side transport residuals).
title: Callable cycle returns stand outside the one-return-contract rule: disagreeing forms can still demote to Continue
